opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government; ordinarily resident in Scotland with at least two years of secondary schooling/college in Scotland or a substantial recent connection to Scotland; entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain, or be an asylum seeker; not eligible for public funds towards tuition fees; enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish HEI. Second-degree applicants must meet additional reskilling criteria.
opportunities.summary: Covers the cost of tuition fees (up to £1,820 per year) for undergraduate degree courses at eligible Scottish higher education institutions for students from low-income households who are not eligible for government funding for their tuition fees. Applications open 1 June 2026 to 1 December 2026 for academic year 2026-27.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households who have been accepted onto the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh); ordinarily resident in Scotland; entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK; have drawn down SAAS living-cost loan or can demonstrate how they will cover living costs; not eligible for public grant funding towards the course; not already obtained a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: A partnership between Carnegie Education Fund and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh providing full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus a £1,200 living-cost bursary, to widen participation in postgraduate study in plant science and botany for Scottish students from low-income households.
